CategoryCount.description: `Slug` is the item's own (leaf) category slug; null counts the items without a category.

CreatePersonaRequest.description: Every field but the name and icon is optional. Seasons default to all four, formality to 1-5.

CreateUploadUrlResponse.description: PUT the photo to `UploadUrl` with exactly `Headers` before `ExpiresAt`, then call `process`.

DailyOutfitResponse.description:
`Outfit` is null only when nothing wearable could be built (then `Message` says so). `WardrobeEmpty` means the outfits
are catalog shopping ideas (`kind` Shopping, `completeness` CatalogOnly). `Weather` is the forecast used, if any.

EventItem.description:
One event as the app sends it. `AnonymousId` is the device's pre-login ID; it is required while the caller is anonymous and
recommended after login. `Properties` is a flat object whose keys depend on `Name` (AnalyticsEventCatalog).

HowToWearResponse.description:
`Outfits` are built around the anchor (in every outfit with `role` Anchor), wardrobe pieces first; gaps come from the catalog
within the persona's budget, each with its cheapest offer, and `completionPrice` sums them. A product the user already owns is
anchored as the wardrobe item. `Message` explains an empty list or catalog-only ideas.

LoginRequest.description: `AnonymousId` is the analytics ID the app used before login; its earlier events are attached to the user.

LogoutRequest.description: `ExpoPushToken` is the phone's push token; when given, that device stops receiving pushes for this account.

NotificationResponse.description: `Status` tells the app whether the push went out; the feed shows `Pending`, `Sent` and `Suppressed` alike.

OfferResponse.description:
`GoPath` (`/api/v1/go/{offerId}`) is the only way to open an offer: the redirect records the click and adds the affiliate
parameters. The seller's own URL is never part of the response.

OutfitCompleteness.description: How much of the outfit the user already owns. Honesty about gaps is part of the contract with the app.

OutfitFeedbackRequest.description:
`Action`: Save, Dismiss, Worn or Shuffle. Save, Dismiss and Worn do what their own endpoints do; Shuffle ("another one") is only
recorded. `Reason` is for Dismiss only (default Other).

OutfitOfferResponse.description: A catalog piece's cheapest offer when it was suggested. `GoPath` is the only way to open it (the click is recorded).

OutfitPieceResponse.description:
One piece. A wardrobe piece has `WardrobeItemId` and its thumbnail; a catalog piece (`Role` Gap, or an Anchor from the
catalog) has `ProductId`, the product image and `Offer`.

OutfitResponse.description:
An outfit. `CompletionPrice` is what the gap pieces cost (their cheapest offers, effective price), null when there are none;
`AnchorPrice` is the catalog anchor's price; `TotalPrice` both together. `Rule` names why it works.

OutfitWeatherResponse.description: The forecast the outfit was built for. `TemperatureC` is the day's dressing temperature, `(2·max + min) / 3`.

PreferencesResponse.description: What the preference endpoints return. Quiet hours are `HH:mm` local times in string PreferencesResponse.TimeZone.

PriceSummary.description: Computed over in-stock prices only: the lowest of the active offers now, and the extremes seen in snapshots.

ProductListItem.description: Prices and `CheapestSeller` are those of the product's lowest active, in-stock offer. `MatchScore` (0-100) is present only when the request named a persona.

ProductResponse.description: `MatchScore` is present when the request named a persona; `SizeHint` when the caller is signed in. Both are left out otherwise.

ProductSummary.description: The few product fields every engagement list shows next to its own data. `LowestPrice` is null when nothing can be bought.

PushDelivery.description: What Expo said about one message (one notification to one device). `Status` is `ok`, `error` or `unreachable`.

PutSellerRequest.description:
The seller. `Name`, `Kind`, `WebsiteUrl` and `IsActive` are replaced on every PUT. The affiliate fields are the
exception, because workers that only know the shop would otherwise wipe what was configured by hand: left out = unchanged, an explicit
null (or blank) = cleared. The `*Set` flags record which of them the body contained; the JSON reader only calls an init accessor
for a property that is present.

RecordWearRequest.description: `WornOn` defaults to today in Europe/Istanbul. The body may be left out entirely.

RegisterRequest.description: `AnonymousId` is the analytics ID the app used before registering; its earlier events are attached to the new user.

SavedProductItem.description:
The catalog's ProductListItem fields, flattened, plus `isActive` (saved products stay in the list after they
are delisted) and `savedAt`. A product nobody sells has `offerCount` 0 and `lowestPrice` 0.

SellerRef.description: The seller of the offer that defines `lowestPrice`, for the "from X" label next to the price.

SendTestResponse.description: The notification as the push sender left it, and what Expo said about each device it was sent to.

SizeHintResponse.description:
Which size to buy. `Size`, `Source` and `Confidence` are the user's own entry for the product's brand and group, when
there is one. Without it `Suggestion` may carry a guess from the user's sizes at other brands (not stored).

SizeSuggestion.description: A guess, not stored anywhere: what the user probably wears at a brand they have not told us about.

StoredAnalysis.description: What is kept of a vision answer in `AnalysisJson`: everything except the images and the embedding (stored on their own).

StyleCardsResponse.description: `Remaining` counts the unswiped cards that did not fit into this response.

StyleFamily.description: The broad style families a style card (and, heuristically, a product) belongs to.

StyleResponse.description: The whole derived style profile, weights included. For debugging and the app's "tarzın" screen.

StyleSummary.description: What the app shows about a persona's learned taste. `TopColors` has up to 3 names, `TopFamilies` up to 2.

SubmitSwipesResponse.description: `OnboardingCompleted` turns true once any persona has reached int SubmitSwipesEndpoint.OnboardingLikes likes.

SweepOffersRequest.description: The body is optional; without a seller the whole catalog is swept.

TriggerResponse.description: `AlertId` is null once the alert has been deleted.

UpdateAlertRequest.description: A partial update: a null field is left as it is. `Sizes: []` clears the size filter.

UpdateItemRequest.description:
A partial update: a null field is left as it is, and `Clear` names the optional fields to empty (IReadOnlyList<string> UpdateItemRequest.ClearableFields).
An empty body is valid: it is the one-tap "looks right" confirmation. Enum values are names, matched case-insensitively.

UpdatePersonaRequest.description:
A partial update: a null field is left as it is, and a given list replaces the stored one (`[]` clears preferred/avoided
lists, but not seasons). `ClearBudget: true` removes both budget bounds.

UpdatePreferencesRequest.description:
A partial update: a null field is left as it is. Quiet hours are `HH:mm` local times in Europe/Istanbul and come as a pair;
`ClearQuietHours: true` removes them.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Replaces the measurements: a field that is left out is cleared. `Audience` is the exception, a null keeps the current one
(a profile always has an audience). `City` (at most 80 characters; blank clears it) is where the outfit engine reads the weather.

UpsertItemResult.description: An item that was stored: the IDs let a worker reconcile its own records with ours.

VisionColor.description: `Name` is a `ProductColor` name; `Hex` the measured shade.

WardrobeGap.description: `CategorySlug` is the top-level category of the missing piece (`ust-giyim`, ...).

WardrobeGapsResponse.description:
`PersonaId` is the persona the analysis was made for (the active one, else the first), or null for a user without personas.
`SuggestedProducts` fill the first gap: catalog items of its category, color and formality band, active and in stock, not
already in the wardrobe, and with a persona a `matchScore` of at least int GetGapsEndpoint.MinMatchScore.

WardrobeItemResponse.description:
One wardrobe item. `ThumbUrl`/`CutoutUrl` are public and permanent (a catalog item whose image could not be copied shows the
catalog's image); `OriginalUrl` is a 15-minute presigned link, given only when there is no cutout to show. `NeedsCategory`
asks the app to let the user pick one of `Analysis.CategoryCandidates`. `Analysis` is there once a photo was analysed.

WardrobeItemSummary.description: An item in lists (the wardrobe grid, the stats' most and least worn).

WardrobeStatsResponse.description:
Over the wardrobe (not archived, not failed). An item counts as unworn for 180 days when its last wear, or its creation when it was
never worn, is more than 180 days ago. `PossibleOutfits` is the outfit engine's count of complete, wearable core outfits (top,
bottom, shoes) the wardrobe makes, capped at 999 (see `OutfitCounter`); never null since Task 12.

WearResponse.description: `WornOn` is the day just recorded, or null after an undo.
